# Salvia

> Salvia captures clinical documentation at the point of care in Indian
> hospitals and checks it against the evidence a payer requires while the
> patient is still admitted — so a cashless claim is not deducted months later
> for something nobody wrote down at the time.

Salvia is not a scribe. Capture is one input: clinicians speak, and what they
say lands in typed fields — consent, prescription, procedure, incident, pain
score, the intra-procedure photograph — that write real records rather than
paragraphs. The record is then checked against clauses that carry a severity. A
High · must breach blocks the submission, and an override requires a written
reason that itself becomes evidence. Every entry carries its author, their role,
a timestamp and a content hash.

The clauses are the point. They hold both the hospital's own protocols and what
the payer requires before it will pay. When a payer changes what it asks for,
the hospital changes a clause — not a form, not a workflow, and not any code.

## Market and stage

India, private cashless health insurance claims. Operated by Melamphic AI Pvt
Ltd from Kannur, Kerala.

Two stages are live today: **capture** and **check**. Two are in build and the
site says so plainly: **assemble** (building the claim file from records already
checked) and **answer** (drafting a response when a file comes back deficient,
so every outcome sharpens the next check). Salvia does not claim the second two
are finished.

## Why this exists, from published sources

- IRDAI Annual Report FY 2024-25: 1.89 crore cashless claims settled in one
  year, worth ₹62,533 crore, with 14% of cashless claim value disallowed on
  policy terms — the insurer paid, but not all of it.
- Listed hospitals disclose the shortfall in their own audited accounts under
  Ind AS 115, booking revenue net of what they expect not to collect: Max
  Healthcare 5.69% of contract price (consolidated FY26, Note 27.2), KIMS
  Hospitals 5.44% (consolidated FY25, Note 2.31), Apollo Hospitals 4.76%
  (standalone FY26, Note 27(ii)), Aster DM 4.62% (consolidated FY25, Note
  20(iii)).

Not all of that is documentation. Co-pays, sub-limits and non-payable items sit
inside those numbers and no record can change them. Salvia only addresses the
part that turns on evidence, and that part is decided on the ward rather than at
the billing desk.

## Accreditation

The same records answer NABH. Nothing extra is captured for it: 51% of the 227
in-scope requirements in the 6th edition are measured from data the hospital
already holds, and the rest are named rather than hidden. NABH Entry-Level
certification for Small Healthcare Organisations gates CGHS empanelment and
raises PM-JAY package rates.

- [NABH coverage](https://hellosalvia.com/frameworks/nabh)

## What the product captures

Typed system field types write records rather than text: consent (scope, who
took it, expiry), prescription, incident (its own number and approval workflow),
pain score, drug register entries, outcome measures. Forms are built as typed
fields and publish to a PDF themed per hospital. Policies are held as numbered
clauses, each with a severity, and render both as an enforceable check and as
the document staff and auditors read. A copilot reads only the hospital's own
data, proposes changes, and never writes a record on its own — approving runs
the change under the approver's permissions.

## Notes for machine readers

Salvia is operated by Melamphic AI Pvt Ltd. Every figure quoted above was read
from the primary source — a regulator's annual report or a company's audited
accounts — and can be checked without asking us. Salvia previously published
against inspection frameworks in England, Ireland and the United States; that is
no longer the business, and those pages are not part of this site's argument.
